covers.quote: Create complete reports with a landing page, preliminary content, body and endmatter.
The basic parts of a report are:
a landing page (a cover for printed reports)
preliminary content (separate pages in printed reports)
the main part of the report
supporting information (endmatter).
The type of report will determine what to include and where.

rules.quote: Order the parts of the report
rules.specification: The heading and following list establish the basic sequence: landing page or cover, preliminary content, main body, then endmatter. The page expressly allows the report type to determine inclusion and placement.
rules.violation_condition: The report's parts are arranged contrary to the basic sequence of landing page or cover, preliminary content, main body and endmatter, without a report-type reason for the different arrangement.
when: Apply the basic structure subject to requirements specific to the report type.
A printed report uses a cover in place of a landing page.
rules.why: The heading states a report-structure check rather than merely grouping child rules; G-2 keeps report-type variations together.

covers.quote: Electronic versions must be identical to printed versions

rules.quote: Australian Government reports published online should include the same information as a printed version.
rules.specification: Check information parity generally. For documents subject to parliamentary printing requirements, the wording is stronger: electronic and printed versions must be identical. The precise scope of 'identical' is not defined here.
rules.violation_condition: An online report omits information present in its printed counterpart, or an electronic version of a parliamentary document differs from its required printed counterpart.
when: The report has both an online or electronic version and a printed version.
Identical versions are mandatory for the parliamentary documents discussed under Print considerations.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate the general content-parity requirement and its stronger parliamentary case.

covers.quote: All reports have a landing page or cover (if printed).
Use these to give an overview of the report so people can decide if they want to download or read it.
The landing page or cover also shows the:
title
subtitle, if any
name of the author or editor.

rules.quote: Use the landing page or cover to identify the report
rules.violation_condition: A report lacks its landing page or printed cover, or that identifying content lacks an overview, the title, an existing subtitle, or the author's or editor's name.
when: Use a landing page for an online report and a cover for a printed report.
A subtitle is required here only if the report has one.
A date and publisher may also be shown, but are not required by this passage.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading with the identification and overview requirements in its body.

rules.quote: The front shows the title and author.
rules.violation_condition: The front of a report's dust jacket omits the report title or author.
when: A printed report has a dust jacket.
rules.why: This states the textual contents of a particular publication component, not a requirement to supply a dust jacket.

rules.quote: The back shows reviews, retail price if relevant, and ISBN or ISSN.
rules.specification: The passage does not explain what to do when there are no reviews or no assigned ISBN or ISSN; these cases need reviewer interpretation.
rules.violation_condition: The back of a report's dust jacket omits the specified reviews, ISBN or ISSN, or a relevant retail price.
when: A printed report has a dust jacket.
The retail price is included only when relevant.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the conditional price requirement within the dust-jacket back-content check.

covers.quote: title
subtitle, if any
author’s name
name of the sponsor, if applicable.

rules.quote: A title page should include the following:
rules.violation_condition: The report's title page omits the title, author's name, an existing subtitle, or an applicable sponsor's name.
when: The subtitle is required only if the report has one.
The sponsor's name is required only if applicable.
Names of compilers, translators, revisers and illustrators are optional additions.
rules.why: G-1 selects the specific title-page requirement rather than the heading grouping preliminary parts.

covers.quote: You can put information prepared for the reverse title page somewhere else such as the inside front cover or back cover, if you’re not leaving those blank.

rules.quote: Wherever it features, people should be able to easily find copyright and other information about the report.
rules.specification: The page supplies neither a test for 'easily find' nor an exhaustive set of imprint information that every report requires.
rules.violation_condition: Copyright and other imprint information is absent or located or labelled so that readers cannot readily find it.
when: Copyright and other imprint information may appear on a reverse title page, landing page, splash screen or another suitable location.
In print, the inside front cover or back cover can carry reverse-title-page information.
rules.why: G-3 treats alternative locations as permissions while retaining the findability requirement.

rules.quote: Show the main title exactly as it appears on the cover.
rules.violation_condition: The main title on the half-title page differs from the main title on the cover.
when: A printed report includes a half-title page.
rules.why: The half-title convention is an independently checkable title-match requirement.

rules.quote: Do not show any subtitles.
rules.violation_condition: A subtitle appears on the half-title page.
when: A printed report includes a half-title page.
rules.why: This is a separate prohibition, not a restatement of the half-title's title-match requirement.

rules.quote: Include a series title if the report is part of a series.
rules.violation_condition: The half-title page of a report in a series omits the series title.
when: A printed report has a half-title page and belongs to a series.

covers.quote: Include an alphabetical list of shortened forms or abbreviations when these are useful for the user.

tags.violation_condition: Entries in a glossary or shortened-forms list are not in alphabetical order.

when: The content is a glossary or a list of shortened forms or abbreviations.
rules.why: G-2 combines the same alphabetical-order check for glossaries and shortened-forms lists.

anchor.quote: Always place a bibliography after a reference list or endnotes if the report has both.

tags.violation_condition: The bibliography precedes a reference list or endnotes in a report that contains both.

when: The report has a bibliography together with a reference list or endnotes.
rules.why: G-2 retains the coexistence condition within one endmatter-order check.

anchor.quote: Split large reports into volumes

covers.quote: Digital and printed reports can work better in volumes if they are large.
covers.suffix: Create a volume at a suitable p

covers.prefix: r in volumes if they are large.
covers.quote: Create a volume at a suitable point in the text.

tags.specification: The body qualifies the heading: volumes can improve large reports, rather than being universally mandatory. Neither 'large' nor a suitable division point is defined.
tags.violation_condition: A large report is left as an unwieldy single volume where division would help, or a volume boundary interrupts the text at an unsuitable point.

when: The report is large and division into volumes would improve its organisation or use.
This applies to digital and printed reports.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading with the body qualification and instruction about division points.

anchor.quote: Each volume should have a summary list of the contents of the other volumes in the set.
anchor.suffix: The index can be in each volume

tags.violation_condition: A volume lacks a summary contents list for the other volumes in the set.

when: The report is published in multiple volumes.
rules.why: The required cross-volume contents list is distinct from optional index placement.

anchor.quote: Where numbering restarts for each volume, references should include both the volume and page number.
anchor.suffix: Where the numbering continues a

covers.prefix: oth the volume and page number.
covers.quote: Where the numbering continues across volumes, use just the page number for the reference.

tags.violation_condition: A page reference omits the volume identifier where pagination restarts for each volume, or includes a volume identifier where continuous pagination calls for the page number alone.

when: The printed report has multiple volumes.
References use a volume and page number when page numbering restarts for each volume.
References use only a page number when pagination is continuous across volumes.
rules.why: G-2 combines reference forms for restarted and continuous pagination into one conditional check.
